scope: Reader guide for the P1–P15 folding and late-scan line. Ratios below 1 favour the named phase over direct sparse ANF only at the stated measurement boundary. The guide does not turn mechanism, semantic, or predecessor improvements into a performance or production claim.
public_audit_boundary: This site publishes the compact ledger, this guide, and P15's final disposition. The detailed P1–P14 local audit bundles are identified by artifact name but are not public downloads from this site.

studies.change: Added profitability-aware folding on frozen natural cones.
studies.tested: Whether natural cones contain folds worth taking.
studies.lesson: No natural folds were accepted (0 of 28 candidates); an apparent generic-comparator result was abstention and optimizer overhead, not a fold win.

studies.change: Moved planning inline onto the original source DAG.
studies.tested: Whether eliminating a separately executed rewrite changes the source-inclusive outcome.
studies.lesson: Natural folds remained zero, so inline planning still added overhead without recovered lowering work.

studies.change: Fused shallow folding with demand-driven discovery.
studies.tested: Whether only building plans demanded by lowering avoids inactive work.
studies.lesson: The constructed Gate-P family exercised 58 folds, but natural cones still accepted none and matching/control cost exceeded saved ANF work.

studies.tested: Whether a stronger algebraic contraction can make lowering cheaper.
studies.disposition: MECHANISM PASS — NOT A PRODUCTION RESULT
studies.lesson: The constructed mechanism family shows a real lower-stage contraction, but Python metadata construction dominated the full path.

studies.change: Packed construction metadata and demand arithmetic.
studies.tested: Whether cheaper metadata recovers P4's full-path cost.
studies.lesson: Packing removed much of P4's construction tax but still did not cross the direct source-inclusive gate.

studies.change: Stored two semantic words in every node.
studies.tested: Whether metadata locality is cheaper than the P5 representation.
studies.lesson: Moving the metadata into nodes did not remove the construction cost needed for a direct crossover.

studies.tested: Whether a lower-level annotation representation improves the complete path.
studies.lesson: The buffer representation was slower than P6's in-node representation at the relevant boundary.

studies.change: Added a formula-level probe before annotation.
studies.tested: Whether dispatching the annotation work selectively is cheaper.
studies.lesson: Probe cost and false-positive annotations outweighed the work avoided; this corrected the original P7 timing interpretation.

studies.change: Froze a zero-pass telemetry tree for dispatch.
studies.tested: Whether a no-traversal policy can preserve decisions without a source scan.
studies.lesson: Correctness and zero-pass policy invariance held, but the source-inclusive direct gate still did not pass.

studies.change: Reduced the tree to seven frozen counters.
studies.tested: Whether minimal telemetry removes enough P8 overhead.
studies.lesson: P9 improved over P8 but remained above direct.

studies.change: Fused minimal telemetry into source construction.
studies.tested: Whether avoiding a separate counter pass changes the direct comparison.
studies.lesson: Fusing counters helped versus P9, but the confidence interval still included parity.

studies.tested: Whether threshold-specific work removes the remaining engineering tax.
studies.lesson: Specialization improved telemetry but did not establish a direct-baseline win.

studies.change: Added lazy reuse scanning and derived pair statistics.
studies.tested: Whether exactification can be made rare enough to win overall.
studies.lesson: Most scans were avoided and a workload-weighted crossover appeared, but the preregistered case-balanced endpoint remained above direct.

studies.tested: Whether deferring pair work removes P12's residual metadata tax.
studies.lesson: The direct endpoint remained above parity and no clear gain over P12 was established.

studies.change: Ran sealed prospective exact-dispatch evaluation with retained exposed encodings.
studies.tested: Whether the exact dispatcher beats direct lowering on sealed synthetic and natural corpora.
studies.lesson: Five rare synthetic encodings were worth retaining as correctness exposures, but the overall exact dispatcher lost to direct on both corpora.

studies.change: Replaced the observer clone with a late exact scan over the owned complete factory arena.
studies.tested: Whether the redesign preserves the decision contract without discarding factory history.
studies.lesson: The sealed fresh-corpus semantic check passed (384 synthetic and 106 natural cases). Zero timing artifacts were accepted, so no timing estimand, performance result, or production recommendation exists.
